title: Reduce GPU workspace and memory use via activation checkpointing, scratch buffer consolidation, and arena tuning
author: Priya Raman
description: Context: High-memory workloads (long sequences and dense batching) expose fragmentation and transient workspace peaks in the GPU runtime. These peaks increase instance sizing and reduce effective throughput for customers. This PR reduces steady-state and peak device memory by combining: 1) selective activation checkpointing for large transformer blocks, 2) consolidation/reuse of temporary scratch buffers across kernels, and 3) arena allocator tuning to reduce fragmentation for small/medium allocations. Motivation: Give customers better GPU utilization without changing model weights or serving semantics. Changes are opt-in via runtime flags and default to conservative settings to avoid regressions. Checklist: - [x] Microbenchmarks for 8k/16k tokens showing memory and latency impact - [x] Integration tests for KV cache and streaming workloads - [x] CI success (linux/gpu) after two reruns - [x] Canary rollout plan for Dedicated pools Overview of changes (high level): - Add per-layer activation checkpointing hook and heuristics to choose checkpointed layers based on activation size and compute cost. Checkpointing reduces peak memory by trading extra forward/back recomputation for lowered memory usage. - Introduce a shared scratch buffer manager that fingerprints kernel temporary sizes and reuses a per-stream buffer instead of allocating per-kernel scratch on demand. - Tune the GPU arena allocator: reduce min-slab size, increase slab coalescing window, and add a fast-path for repeated small allocations used by KV cache and attention kernels. - Update the scheduler's memory-aware packing heuristic so continuous-batching will avoid combining two requests that would exceed tuned workspace limits. - Add config knobs (runtime flags and console-visible settings) and documentation. Performance summary: - Peak device memory reduced by 18-28% on our standard 8k token transformer perf test across V100/A100/RTX6000 profiles (28% on A100 with mixed-precision and large batches). - Scratch buffer allocations dropped ~40% in number and total scratch footprint reduced by ~33% on average. - End-to-end P99 latency impact: +2-6% in worst-case for checkpointed workloads (configurable), throughput improved 8-12% for memory-bound scenarios due to better packing. - No observable regression for small-sequence (<1k) fast-path in standard CI. Backward compatibility: Changes are opt-in and guarded by flags; defaults chosen to be conservative. Migration notes: For Dedicated customers we will run an opt-in canary; Private installer has a new config option to enable aggressive tuning. Related: ENG-8274 (memory-constrained serving), SUP-412 (customer incident: out-of-memory on large-batch inference).

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Can we make the checkpointing heuristic opt-out per model? I prefer that for large customers so they can tune per-model.
Priya Raman (author): Yes, added a per-model annotation and runtime flag. Default remains heuristic-driven.
Anna Liu: Need a guard in the arena allocator for pathological alloc/free patterns we saw in stress tests.
Priya Raman: Added a fast-path and an integration test that reproduces the pattern; CI validated it.
Samir Patel: CI noisy failure on the first gpu pipeline run (OOM) — reran and it passed. Documented in CI checks.
QA (J. Thompson): KV cache correctness validated under checkpointing; no cache invalidations observed.
merge_summary: Merged by squash-merge after approvals from Diego and Anna. Release notes entry added. Canary rollout scheduled for Dedicated pools next week.
release_notes: Reduce GPU peak and steady-state memory through activation checkpointing (opt-in), consolidated scratch buffers, and improved arena allocator tuning. Expected memory reduction 18-28% for long-sequence workloads; potential small latency increase for checkpointed flows. Flags available to tune aggressiveness.
canary_plan: Stage 1: internal Dedicated pools (5%) with conservative defaults. Stage 2: increase to 25% for memory-bound customers. Monitor token-level memory and OOM alerts; rollback if >1% error delta.
notes_for_ops: Monitor allocator fragmentation metrics (arena_free_ratio, slab_count) and scratch reuse hit-rate. If customers report unexpected latency regressions, toggle runtime.flags.checkpointing_policy to 'none' for the model and re-evaluate.
acknowledgements: Thanks to infra team for CI pipeline help and to the perf lab for benchmark runs.
